subject: Silverwood v2 candidate — variant compatibility gating question
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intake: Silverwood v2 candidate — quick gating question

Team —

Silverwood just delivered a release candidate (labelled v2-rc) for the Silverwood-S baseline we want to evaluate for Hosted. Their engineering lead attached a short compat matrix and the model card (see attachments). The product ask: can we run a focused compatibility check and give a temporary recommendation about whether we should pin the current production variant or allow v2-rc into canary?

Main risks called out by Silverwood: tokenizer changed slightly (some new control tokens), kv-cache shape is the same but there are different sparse attention patterns for long context, and they shipped a different default quantization-friendly ordering. We don't have a runway to run full evals before next week's partner demo, but we need a safe operating decision for the rollout window.

Asks:
- Dev: short checklist — what are the minimum checks you need to rule out regressions for safety and latency?
- Infra/ops: what telemetry/metrics do we need in canary to detect KV cache blowups and tokenization regressions quickly?
- Product (Priyom): can you weigh in on business tolerance for a provisional pin vs conditional canary?

Attachments: compat-matrix.xlsx, silverwood-model-card.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product, Model Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intake: Silverwood v2 candidate — quick gating question

Thanks Marissa — quick read. High-level ask answered up front: we should NOT let v2-rc into broad canary until we validate tokenization and KV cache behavior on our runtime; however, a very narrow canary (0.5-1% traffic, constrained routes, with strict fallback) could be acceptable if the infra/telemetry constraints below are met.

Minimum checks I need before any canary expansion:
1) Tokenizer sanity: run a 10k sample prompt set (prod prompts + edge cases) and diff token sequences — attach sample-quant-profile.json for the quant differences I expect. If we see >1.5% tokenization drift on prompts with anchors (code, tables), flag for manual review.
2) KV cache pressure test: run synthetic long-context chains (8k, 16k windows) across our GPU fleet and measure peak GPU memory and latency tail (>95th). If memory allocation spikes or >30% latency tail regression, no canary.
3) Quant path functional checks: inference on representative batch sizes (1, 8, 16) and compare logits and top-k distributions vs v1 baseline; tolerate small numeric differences but not behavioral regressions for reranking/generation tasks.

Telemetry/alarms we need in place for any canary:
- Per-variant 95th/99th latency, GPU memory headroom, OOMs (immediate rollback), tokenization drift rate (new metric), generation quality regression score (paired prompt set).
- Auto-fallback: route traffic off within 120s of any OOM spike or 2x baseline error rate.

I can run the tokenization diff and the functional quant checks today if we get the model artifact and a small sample corpus. I will attach sample-quant-profile.json and a short playbook for the KV load test.

--
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachments: sample-quant-profile.json, canary-playbook.md

From: Sarah Lim <sarah@silverwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intake: Silverwood v2 candidate — quick gating question

Hi all — thanks for the quick look. A couple clarifications from our side that might help Dev's checks:
- Tokenizer: the new control tokens are opt-in via a token map; the model will fall back to legacy tokens if the mapping isn't provided. We can provide the token map and a small conversion shim you can drop into your tokenizer test harness.
- KV pattern: we did add localized sparse attention for long contexts to speed up retrieval-heavy prompts; it shouldn't change the KV tensor shape, but it does change internal memory access patterns. We'll share a mini-benchmark and the exact config used for the sparse modules.

We are happy to hold to a narrow, tightly instrumented canary while you run the tests — our partner demo is on June 25th; if you can give a provisional decision by Monday EOD (June 22), that would help.

Thanks,
Sarah
Engineering Lead, Model Delivery
Silverwood AI

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lim <sarah@silverwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intake: Silverwood v2 candidate — quick gating question

Summary and proposal (short):

I agree with Dev's conservative approach. Business side tolerance: product is willing to accept a temporary hold/pin if the tests show material risk to latency or correctness; they prefer a conditional narrow canary if we can guarantee the telemetry and auto-fallback Dev described. The partner demo schedule means we need a provisional stance by Monday.

I propose the following immediate plan:
- Dev: run tokenizer diff and quant functional checks on the 10k prompt sample today/tomorrow. Use the token map Sarah offered. Prioritize the code/table anchors.
- Infra/ops: stand up the canary with strict limits (0.5% traffic, route-level allowlist: "/assistant-code", "/qa-embed"), attach the alarms (95/99 latency, OOMs, tokenization-drift), and enable auto-fallback to current prod variant on alarm.
- Product: I will communicate to GTM that we either (A) allow a limited canary with telemetry and automatic fallback, or (B) pin production to current variant until checks complete.

Decision checkpoint: Monday 2026-06-22 18:00 PDT. If Dev's tests show >1.5% tokenization drift or >30% tail latency degradation we pin. If not, proceed with narrow canary.

I'll coordinate the stakeholder update and add a short note to the canary runbook. Please add any missing checks here.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
--
Forwarded attachments: compat-matrix.xlsx, silverwood-model-card.pdf, sample-quant-profile.json, canary-playbook.md
